frequency_question: What proportion of Senate-confirmed executive nominations complete all procedural confirmation steps within a 49-day calendar window under assumptions of cooperation?
membership_rule: Includes all cabinet, agency head, and commissioner-level nominations officially received by the Senate where floor action is desired; excludes nominations submitted during long congressional recesses where committees do not sit.
provenance_note: claimed 2 hits but 3 of 6 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 6 representative historical instances sampled from legislative tracking databases matching tight calendar windows.
known_gaps: Sample is illustrative of fast-track vs standard friction; exact universe of sub-50 day confirmations is sparsely populated due to rare submission timing.
skeleton: Decomposed into procedural phases: committee questionnaire review (14 days min), FBI/ethics background clearance (10 days min), committee hearing and markup (14 days min), and floor scheduling/vote queue (15 days min). Total minimum sequential days = 53 calendar days.
multiplier: 14 + 10 + 14 + 15 = 53 minimum calendar days required for absolute baseline procedure.
validity_reason: Senate procedural rules and standing committee timelines remain stable across Congresses unless major rule changes (like filibuster or quorum reforms) occur.
